plain_english_policy: Enactment of this bill would create a legal exception to Alabama's ethics laws regarding public employees receiving rewards for good work.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Under current rules, accepting any reward from an outside source could be seen as using one's job for personal gain. This law changes that by stating it is not considered 'personal gain' if three specific conditions are met: 1) The reward was unsolicited (not asked for), 2) Only the person giving the reward believes the service was exemplary, and 3) The state Ethics Commission must be told about the reward before it happens.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Morrow (sponsor) supports clarifying that unsolicited rewards for good service are not unethical.
evidence_quotes: This bill would provide that a public employee who receives a reward from a third party for exemplary public service would not be considered as using his or her official position for personal gain.
A conflict of interest shall exist when... which is uniquely affected by proposed or pending legislation.

No public official or public employee shall use or cause to be used equipment, facilities, time, materials, human labor, or other public property under his or her discretion or control for the private benefit...

A public employee may not be deemed to be using his or her official position for personal gain if a third party wishes to provide a reward for exemplary service by the public employee if each of the following conditions are met: (1) The reward is unsolicited. (2) Solely in the opinion of the rewarding individual or entity, the public employee has provided exemplary public service.
The Ethics Commission is notified by the rewarding individual or entity... prior to the reward being issued.
